name: Rips by Triumph
tagline: 100% fair-market buyback paid in cash, with pack odds shown before you open.
signupOffer: Free card pack with code FHIFKMV

buyback.note: Reported as the highest rate in the category, and paid out as cash rather than site credit in independent testing.

shipping.note: Ship or sell back within a 7-day decision window.

operator: Triumph TCG, LLC (Triumph Labs) - San Francisco, CA
pros: 100% fair-market buyback, the highest rate we found
Buyback reportedly pays cash rather than site credit
Pack odds displayed before you buy
Wide price range from $1 up to $1,000
cons: App only, with no browser version
KYC verification required before you can ship or withdraw
Seven-day window to decide, or the choice is made for you
verdict: The cleanest of the rip apps we looked at. A 100% buyback paid in cash is the thing to look for in this category, and Triumph is the only one on this list reported to do both.

name: PrizePicks Packs
tagline: The biggest name in pick'em launched digital rips in October 2026.
signupOffer: Referral signup offer, Packs sit inside the main app

buyback.note: PrizePicks states cards can be shipped or sold back at fair market value. No fixed percentage published at launch.

shipping.note: Ship the card or sell it back after opening.

pros: By far the most established operator in this category
Odds and potential card values shown before you open
Highest-value inventory of any rip product, including an eight-figure headline card
Already a trusted name if you use it for pick'em
cons: Launched October 2026, so there is no track record yet
Buyback percentage not published at launch
Terms frame it as ecommerce rather than a regulated gambling product
verdict: The name alone makes this the one most people will try first, and an operator this size has far more to lose from mishandling payouts than a startup does. Worth watching rather than committing to until the buyback terms firm up.

name: Crown Rips
tagline: Free $1 welcome pack, 100% buyback into a withdrawable cash balance.

buyback.note: Buyback credits your cash balance, withdrawable after ID verification. The percentage is applied to the operator's own valuation of the card.

shipping.note: Ship or vault. Vaulted cards auto-sell back after 3 days.

pros: Genuine free pack on signup with no deposit
100% buyback into a balance you can actually withdraw
Entry packs start at $1, so it is cheap to try
Top advertised pulls run to around $100,000
cons: Vaulted cards are sold back automatically after only 3 days
100% is of the operator's valuation, not of what the pack cost you
Deposited funds must be played before withdrawal
19+ rather than 18+, and not available in every state
verdict: The free $1 pack makes this the easiest one on the list to try for nothing, and a withdrawable cash balance puts it ahead of the credit-only options. Watch the 3-day vault window, which is the shortest here.

name: Tilt Rips
tagline: 90% buyback with published odds and live market values on every pull.
signupOffer: Free Dollar Pack with code RJCTXH

buyback.note: Sell-back pays 90% of market value. Vault claim window is longer than most rivals.

shipping.note: Shipping can take up to six weeks. Fees shown before you confirm.

pros: Odds and live market values shown on each pull
Longer vault claim window than most competitors
Shipping fees disclosed before you confirm
Well-regarded app design
cons: Shipping can take up to six weeks
90% buyback rather than the 100% the best options pay
App Store rating of 3.6 from 400+ reviews
User complaints centre on support and shipping costs
verdict: Solid transparency on odds and pricing, let down by shipping times measured in weeks. Fine if you plan to sell back rather than ship, which is what most people do anyway.

name: CrownCards
tagline: The most complete odds disclosure of any rip site we looked at.
signupOffer: Bonus pack up to $100 after a $20 deposit, code 4J5CKZGW

buyback.note: No buyback rate published at the time of writing. Confirm before depositing.

pros: The fullest odds disclosure we found in this category
Sells graded cards rather than raw, so valuations are harder to fudge
Bonus pack worth up to $100 on a $20 deposit
cons: No published buyback rate, which is the number that matters most
Launched June 2026, so the track record is short
Despite the name, no connection to Crown Coins or Crown Rips
verdict: Best-in-class odds disclosure, but the missing buyback rate is a real gap. Worth a look if you want to actually keep the cards rather than flip them back.

name: Courtside
tagline: Social sportsbook with a Pokemon rip feature built into the coin economy.
signupOffer: 100 in free play on first purchase, code BZ054001

buyback.note: Cards convert to Courtside Coins, which can then be turned into real cash.

shipping.note: Cards cannot be shipped. Conversion to coins is the only option.

pros: Rips sit alongside a full social sportsbook, so one account covers both
Strong app ratings at 4.7 on iOS and 4.5 on Android
Packs priced in coins, so you can rip using balance you already have
cons: Cards cannot be shipped at all, only converted
Pack odds are not published
Priced in coins rather than dollars, which obscures what a pack really costs
Free play arrives on first purchase, not on signup
verdict: Really a sportsbook with a rip feature attached rather than a rip platform. If you want the card itself, this is the wrong place. If you just want the coin value, it works.

name: Packz
tagline: Publishes pull rates and holds sealed product, with a 90% buyback in site credit.
signupOffer: Scratch card worth $7 or $100 after first pack, code MDPR5JJY
packPrices: Up to $100 on the welcome pack

buyback.note: Standard buyback is paid as non-withdrawable credit usable on more packs, not as cash.

shipping.note: US-only shipping. Unshipped cards auto-sell back after 72 hours.

pros: Publishes pull rates and reportedly holds real sealed product
Welcome pack carries a 100% buyback rather than the standard 90%
One of the longer-running options here, live since September 2025
cons: Standard buyback pays site credit rather than cash
Welcome bonus funds are non-withdrawable and expire in 48 hours
Trustpilot rating of 1.7 against an App Store rating of 4.7
Unshipped cards are sold back automatically after 72 hours
Reports of repeated ID and selfie verification checks
Scratch card reward requires a first pack purchase
verdict: The pull-rate transparency is genuinely good and it has been running longer than most. The catch is the buyback: 90% in credit you can only spend on more packs is not the same as 90% in cash, and the Trustpilot gap is worth reading before you deposit.

name: Pullz
tagline: Shows minimum and maximum card value before purchase, with buyback at market value.
signupOffer: Free card pack with code XBREVTP

buyback.note: Terms reportedly allow buyback offers at, above or below fair market value, including pricing set per user. No fixed percentage is published. The referral link opens the App Store listing, so the code must be entered in the app during signup.

shipping.note: Shipping reported as unavailable to 13 US states.

pros: Shows the minimum and maximum card value before you buy, which most rivals do not
Some users report payouts arriving in under a business day
cons: No fixed buyback percentage published
Terms reportedly permit buyback pricing set per individual user
Heavy volume of withdrawal complaints in recent app reviews
Reported $200 daily withdrawal cap
Shipping unavailable to 13 US states
verdict: The value-range disclosure before purchase is a good idea, but the buyback has no published floor and recent user reviews are dominated by withdrawal problems. Start small and test a withdrawal before building any balance here.
